newsitem.title: USA: CBOT March corn hits new contract low on hog data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT March corn hits new contract low on hog data.

text.p: Expectations that feed demand from the hog industry would decline helped push March corn to a fresh contract low Monday, and other contracts were also lower at midsession, CBOT traders said.
"Mostly, corn is lower on the hogs and pigs numbers," said one floor trader.

On Friday the U.S. Agriculture Department reported that the number of hogs kept for breeding was at 97 percent of the year-ago level. Most in the trade had expected the report to show that breeding herds were expanding.
Losses were limited by heavy buying from Cargill, which purchased 12 million bushels of March, floor sources said.
"Commodity funds are getting short, and the farmer is the big cash long in the corn," one trader said.

Traders said export inspection figures from USDA were also pressuring corn futures. USDA reported Monday that weekly inspections were 29 million bushels. Trade estimates had ranged from 32 to 45 million bushels, floor sources said.
At 1121 CST, corn was trading 1-1/2 to 4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 4 cents at $2.60-1/2.
